text: The sale selection is declared as two operations of rwb-writeoff on /api/recovery/writeoff/v1 with placeholder paths, operation IDs and element names: POST /write-offs/{writeOffId}/sale-selection taking the selection and answering the write-off, and GET /write-offs with the sale state as a filter returning a paged population row; neither is a branch of the published scan (API-S7-001) or the published committee decision (API-S7-002).

Extending either published operation, or leaving the paths to the builder, would invent an interface in a different way and would break the two stories that own them.

text: The hand-off to the debt sale route is the case move SOLD_POST_CHARGEOFF answered to rwb-case, which the parent CaseWorkflow uses to start the debt sale stage on rwb-debtsale, plus this service's published sold-population read; no operation of rwb-debtsale is called, no event is published for the hand-off, and the lots, reserve, award, buyer portal, cap and settled sale stay with S6.

Inventing a REST call or an event name would be a business interface no source has.

text: The WRITEOFF state SOLD_POST_CHARGEOFF is written on the standard record column write_off.state in this service's own transaction, the case route state of the same name is answered to rwb-case and written there, and decision_log_id is not overwritten: the selection's record chains to the approval record through the decision-record library.
why: TSD S7 T3.1 gives write_off no dedicated route-state column and T3.0 gives the standard state column; legacy AC3 says 'the case moves to SOLD_POST_CHARGEOFF', and the case state is rwb-case's while the same value is a WRITEOFF state of TSD S7 T4. One decision_log_id column cannot hold two records, so a chain is the only choice that keeps the approval's reference.
